uncited: What sets these methods apart from standard [3D Gaussian Splatting](1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) is the decoupling of geometric representation from appearance, allowing for explicit material properties (BRDF) or scalar density fields (VEG) rather than baked spherical harmonics [S1, S2, S1, unofficial].
The rendering pipelines for 3D Gaussian Splatting originated from the foundational work on 3DGS, which introduced the tile-based rasterization of 3D Gaussians for real-time novel view synthesis [S1].
The extension to volume encoding and BRDF-based relighting represents a shift from implicit neural fields and baked appearance to explicit, physically interpretable primitives [S1, S2, unofficial].
These methods are primarily used in computer graphics for real-time rendering, digital twins, and scientific visualization [S1][S2, unofficial].
